caseAnalysis.title: Detained HfA surgeons in Beta Town amid HfA's exit to Gamma
caseAnalysis.summary: Nine Swiss Health for All (HfA) surgeons are confined to their residence in Beta Town by armed tribespeople. This followed HfA's announcement that it would end operations there and move personnel to Gamma City. HfA reports the staff cannot leave until it reaches an agreement with tribal leaders on maintaining health services. HfA states it has a strict no-ransom policy. It says its long-term presence is not viable because of depleted funds and reported donor mandates. Beta's Health Minister and the police chief defer the release to tribal leaders. The Swiss Ambassador committed only to ask Bern about special funds for minimal services, including measles support. The German Ambassador referred compromises to Berlin. The tribal council confined talks to its office and advised against contacting the staff until a resolution is reached. The materials include role prompts for both sides, but no role card identifies which side we represent.

issues.text: No role card was supplied. The shared packet contains prompts for both an HfA-supporting negotiator and the Tribal Leader, so our side is unconfirmed.
Sequencing conflicts. HfA insists on release before discussing the dispute. The tribal leader conditions access and resumed operations on HfA first making clear commitments.

Interim funding is uncertain. The Swiss Ambassador committed only to communicate with Bern. The German Ambassador says compromises are beyond her authority. HfA reports donor mandates to move all resources to Gamma.

immediate.text: The HfA team reports its staff are detained in their residence until an agreement with tribal leaders on health service maintenance is reached. The delegation was told to await further guidance at its hotel.

actors.text: HfA states that safe release is its immediate goal. It also says long-term presence is not viable and that it keeps a no-ransom policy.
The tribal leader restricts talks to the council office. He advises against contacting the staff until an amicable resolution is reached.
Beta's Health Minister says the matter largely rests with tribal leaders. She warns that government interference might escalate tensions.
The local police chief says police will not intervene, fearing clashes. He says police will step in to restore peace once a health services agreement is reached.
The Swiss Ambassador will ask Bern about special funds for minimal health services as a release compromise. He cautioned against paying any ransoms.
FWB and CPI pledge support for the release, including FWB's rapport with tribal leaders.

tension.text: HfA says it stands firm on redeploying to Gamma because funds are depleted. Tribal leaders tie release to commitments on maintaining health services.

background.text: HfA announced the transfer of its Country Director and its Beta Town personnel to Gamma City.

uncertainty.text: The HfA team fears ransom demands and unpredictable actions by local guards if a solution is not found promptly.
Whether Bern or Berlin will approve any interim funding is unresolved.
Our represented side is not established by any role card.

tradeoffs.proposal: Minimal hospital services, such as measles support, funded by possible Swiss special funds
tradeoffs.benefit: The Swiss Ambassador frames this as a compromise to facilitate release without ransom.
tradeoffs.risk: Bern has not approved the funds. The German position favours relocation. The Swiss Ambassador doubts that scaling down helps.

tradeoffs.proposal: A handover to a government-led framework with suitable partners
tradeoffs.benefit: The district administrator supports the transition and is ready to collaborate.
tradeoffs.risk: The administrator wants tribal leaders excluded. The Minister fears the government cannot fill the void.

negotiation_issues.title: Sequencing of staff release versus HfA commitments

decision.text: Whether release precedes or follows commitments on health services.

counterpart_position.text: The tribal leader says access and resumed operations follow HfA's clear commitments.
The HfA delegation insisted on release before discussing the sources of the dispute.

counterpart_reasons.text: HfA says it is hard to address concerns while staff are confined, and that release would let operations resume in the near term.

conditions.text: Staff have been detained for several days. One member may go out daily for necessities.
Talks are restricted to the council office. Contact with staff is discouraged until resolution.

previous_alternatives.text: An unscheduled visit to the residence was refused by the local commander, who lacked directives from tribal leaders and demanded the delegation leave.
HfA declined the Swiss offer of Federal Police negotiators.

decision.text: Whether any compensation can be distinguished from ransom.

counterpart_position.text: Guards say HfA must recognize the distress and unfairness its decision to leave caused the community. They defer the release decision to tribal leaders.

counterpart_reasons.text: HfA says paying ransom in one region might prompt demands elsewhere.

conditions.text: The Swiss Ambassador cautioned against paying any ransoms to local mafias.

dependencies.text: Linked to: Sequencing of staff release versus HfA commitments.

people_interests_power.text: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator says rural security is managed by tribal chiefs with minimal government or military intervention.

pressures_disagreements.text: The UN advises caution about local security personnel and some tribespeople, describing them as unpredictable and potentially dangerous.

no_agreement_consequences.text: HfA fears ransom demands and guard unpredictability without a prompt solution.

coverage_gaps: The tribal chief's four specific demands (restarting hospital activities, continuing operations in Beta Town, compensating guards' families, reinforcing measles response capacity) appear only in document summaries, not in extracted claims.
The Source 24 informant-relayed tribespeople message about extracting maximum support is not extracted as a claim.
Compensation amounts, the September closure date and measles case figures are not in the extracted claims.
No original_priority_text passages were supplied, so extraction coverage could not be checked against the original source text.
